claims.claim: Under Law 20.446 (from 2026) new residents with 183+ days' presence can exempt foreign capital income for the arrival year plus 10

sources.name: IMI Daily: Uruguay raises tax holiday threshold to US$2 million, taxes foreign income at 12%
sources.says: Dated 25 February 2026. Ley 20.446 (budget 2025–2029), from 1 January 2026: new residents get a full exemption on foreign-sourced capital income for "the year of acquisition plus ten calendar years", then a five-year transition at 6%, half the 12% IRPF rate; physical presence over 183 days a year is a route needing no investment; the alternatives are real estate above UI 12.5M (about US$2M) or US$100,000 a year into the innovation fund; the permanent 7% option is being phased out for new residents; holders' "foreign-sourced capital income and gains" fall within the exemption.

sources.name: Funds Society: Uruguay redraws the tax map for international investments
sources.says: Undated (2026). The holiday covers certain foreign capital income "durante el año en que adquieren la residencia y los diez ejercicios siguientes"; conditions include more than 183 days in Uruguay, real estate above UI 12,500,000, or annual investments in productive or innovation funds.

claims.note: Searched the holiday with November 2026: no later change found; Decree 95/026 (May 2026) regulates foreign income in IRPF and does not change the term.

claims.claim: US estate tax applies above the $15M exemption (2026)

sources.name: IRS: What's new, estate and gift tax
sources.says: The table "Basic exclusion amount for year of death" has the row 2026: $15,000,000 (2025: $13,990,000). The page says the Working Families Tax Cuts, Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, "amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026". Page last reviewed or updated 03-Nov-2026.

sources.name: IRS: Estate tax
sources.says: A return is required when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and specific exemption, is more than the filing threshold for the year of death; the table gives 2026: $15,000,000. Page last reviewed or updated 23-Oct-2026.

sources.name: IRS news release IR-2025-103: tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026
sources.says: "Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000", up from $13,990,000 for 2025; the release (October 9, 2025) cites Revenue Procedure 2025-32 and is marked as an archival document.

sources.name: IRS: Some nonresidents with U.S. assets must file estate tax returns
sources.says: "U.S. citizens are subject to U.S. estate taxation with respect to their worldwide assets"; Form 706 is required when worldwide assets plus adjusted taxable gifts exceed the basic exclusion amount in effect on the date of death. By contrast a nonresident who is not a citizen files when US-situated assets exceed $60,000. Page last reviewed or updated 27-Jun-2026.
